papers.title_in_file: Provable Quantum Algorithm Advantage for Gaussian Process Quadrature
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, complexity discussion, Section 6 numerical results text, Section 7 Conclusion; algorithm derivations skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A quantum low-rank Gaussian process quadrature algorithm with a complexity analysis and classical-simulator demonstration.

assertions.value: The authors state that their complexity analysis shows a polynomial advantage over classical Gaussian process quadrature methods.
quotes: we provide a theoretical complexity analysis that shows a polynomial advantage over classical Gaussian process quadrature methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: Complexity analysis in the paper's own Section 5; the advantage is stated against a stated classical baseline and depends on stated assumptions.
assertions.reader_inference: The advantage is polynomial, not exponential, and is relative to the Hilbert-space classical baseline the authors chose.

assertions.value: The authors state that a classical GPQ method with the Hilbert space approximation would cost O(M 3), and so the advantage of the quantum algorithm is polynomial.
quotes: The computational complexity of a GPQ method implemented on a classical computer with the Hilbert space method would be O(M 3) and hence, the advantage is polynomial.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Introduction; the quantum cost it is compared to depends on the data-loading assumption.
assertions.reader_inference: The classical baseline is the paper's choice; the quantum complexity differs by whether data are given as quantum data or classically.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method was demonstrated with numerical simulations of a quantum computer on a classical processor, and that it is suitable for a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
quotes: We provide the numerical simulation of our proposed solution for quantum low-rank Gaussian process quadrature in a classical processor that simulates a quantum computer
The proposed quantum algorithm is suitable for a fault-tolerant quantum computer with enough quantum registers to implement the algorithm precisely.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7 and the Introduction state the paper's own setup and scope.
assertions.reader_inference: No run on quantum hardware is reported.

assertions.value: The authors report that the quantum method showed greater fluctuation than the classical methods in the simulations, which they attribute to limited qubits, finite shots and small rotations.
quotes: the quantum method has greater fluctuation than the classical methods, mainly attributed to the limited amount of qubits used in the simulations, the finite amount of shots, and the small rotations implemented in the algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulation study; the attribution is the authors' own.

papers.title_in_file: Distributed Quantum Gaussian Processes for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, experimental setup and results text, Section 5 Conclusion; algorithm details skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A distributed quantum Gaussian process method with a Riemannian ADMM optimizer, tested on a classical quantum simulator.

assertions.value: The authors report that, aggregated across the SRTM elevation environments, DQGP achieves 32.4% lower NRMSEtest than FACT-GP.
quotes: DQGP achieves 32.4%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a quantum simulator, averaged over replications per the paper's setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against classical distributed GP baselines, not against a quantum-hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the synthetic quantum-GP-prior dataset DQGP achieves on average 47.0% lower NRMSEtest than FACT-GP.
quotes: For the synthetic dataset, DQGP achieves on average 47.0%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on a dataset generated by quantum Gaussian processes.
assertions.reader_inference: The data are drawn from a quantum GP prior, which may favor a quantum kernel.

assertions.value: The authors state that all experiments run on classical quantum state vector simulators, and that the complexity analysis on a simulator does not represent the true complexity on current NISQ hardware, so the work does not include complexity analysis.
quotes: All numerical experiments are conducted using classical quantum state vector simulators in Qiskit and PennyLane

The computational complexity analysis on a quantum simulator run on classical hardware does not represent the true complexity on current NISQ quantum hardware, hence this work does not involve complexity analysis.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of setup and scope in the Section 4 setup paragraph.
assertions.reader_inference: Abstract speedup language is therefore not supported by an analysis in this paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that in some small-data, many-agent cases FACT-GP yields lower NRMSEtest than DQGP, and attribute the gap to the high-dimensional mapping of sparse data using expressive quantum kernels.
quotes: FACT-GP yields lower NRMSEtest than DQGP.
The rare performance gap stems from the high-dimensional mapping of sparse data using expressive quantum kernels.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation with the authors' explanation.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Methodology, Section 5 experimental text, hardware limitations, Conclusion; result figures and tables not read as images
papers.what_it_is: Two hybrid quantum-classical optimal multi-agent pathfinding algorithms that solve QUBO subproblems, run on simulated annealing and a D-Wave annealer.

assertions.value: The authors state that they present the first optimal hybrid quantum-classical MAPF algorithms, and that experiments suggest their approach dominates previous QUBO formulations.
quotes: we present the first optimal hybrid quantum-classical MAPF algorithms
Experiments on actual quantum hardware and results on benchmark data suggest that our approach dominates previous QUBO
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim in the abstract; the supporting numbers are in figures.
assertions.reader_inference: Figure data were not read; the dominance claim is the authors' summary.

assertions.value: The authors state a contribution of an optimality criterion with proof, and that the QCP algorithm is only guaranteed to generate an optimal path set if the QUBO is solved to optimality in every step.
quotes: An optimality criterion with proof, generalizing the pricing problem of classical column generation,
It is only guaranteed to generate an optimal path set if the QUBO is solved to optimality in every step.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proof stated in the Methodology (Section 4.1); the guarantee condition is stated in Section 4.
assertions.reader_inference: The guarantee holds only under an exact QUBO solver, which an annealer is not.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given qubit capacity, connectivity and noise, considering problems with more than 100 agents would lead to unreasonable results on current hardware.
quotes: considering problems with more than 100 agents would thus lead to unreasonable results to the aforementioned limitations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit on problem size in Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that hardware-aware design of the QUBO problems can already lead to an advantage on near-term quantum devices.
quotes: hardware-aware design of the QUBO problems can already lead to an advantage on near-term quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author conclusion; the advantage is over earlier QUBO formulations, not over classical solvers.
assertions.reader_inference: The advantage claimed is relative to previous QUBO formulations on the same kind of device.

papers.title_in_file: Hierarchical Learning for Quantum ML: Novel Training Technique for Large-Scale Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 3.1, 3.2, 4 hardware text, Section 5 Discussion; appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A hierarchical training method for quantum circuit Born machines, tested in GPU simulation up to 27 qubits and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report training a QCBM to load a 3-dimensional multivariate Gaussian distribution on 27 qubits with 1000 parameters on GPU machines, achieving 4% accuracy in TV distance.
quotes: to load a 3-dimensional multivariate Gaussian distribution on 27 qubits
enabled us to effectively train QCBMs with 27 qubits and 1000 parameters on GPU machines, achieving an impressive 4% accuracy in TV distance
assertions.certainty_reason: One numerical study by the vendor authors, run on classical GPU simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The target is a Gaussian distribution; the result is a simulation, not a hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for loading a Gaussian distribution on nine qubits, 2D connectivity greatly outperforms qubits arranged on a line.
quotes: finding that 2D connectivity greatly outperforms qubits arranged on a line
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison in one small-scale study.

assertions.value: The authors state that barren plateau arguments do not strictly apply to their setting because the objective function is not tied to an observable.
quotes: Though barren plateau arguments do not strictly apply here due to the objective function not being tied to an observable
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the scope in which its barren-plateau comment applies.
assertions.reader_inference: Claims that the method avoids barren plateaus are therefore empirical observations, not guarantees.

assertions.value: The authors report that on IBM hardware the Fire Opal optimization improved approximation accuracy for the smaller device, and on the larger device the gains were significant for circuits above a two-qubit-gate threshold.
quotes: The outcomes indicated a marked improvement in approximation accuracy when using the Fire Opal optimization.
Here, the enhancements brought about by Fire Opal optimization were particularly significant in circuits that included more than 22 two-qubit gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Small number of hardware runs from one study (best of five repeats per the text).
assertions.reader_inference: The gain depends on a vendor error-suppression product, so it is not a property of the training method alone.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Image Classification: Experiments on Utility-Scale Quantum Computers
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sections 3, 4 (IBM text), 4.3 Summary, Section 5 Discussion; Quantinuum tables not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: Binary image classification on the Honda Scenes Dataset with variational circuits trained classically and run on Quantinuum and IBM hardware up to 72 qubits.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best quantum models in simulation used block amplitude encoding, and that their largest model reached an accuracy of 0.94.
quotes: We find that the best performance in the quantum models is achieved with the BAE loading method.
yielding an accuracy of 0.94.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study on a two-class image task.

assertions.value: The authors report that the best quantum model is slightly worse than a convolutional neural network with fewer parameters but better than a vanilla fully-connected neural network with more weights.
quotes: slightly worse than a convolutional neural network with fewer parameters but better than a vanilla fully-connected neural network with more weights.
assertions.certainty_reason: Comparison against two classical baselines in one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that on IBM Fez, with over 3000 two-qubit gates, the circuit correctly classified 68% of the images, and that the 99th percentile for random guessing would give an accuracy of 65%.
quotes: Impressively, we see that even with over 3000 two-qubit gates, we manage to correctly classify 68% of the images.
the 99th percentile of outcomes for random guessing would lead to an accuracy of 65%
assertions.certainty_reason: Hardware result on a small test set; accuracy declines with depth.
assertions.reader_inference: 68% is only slightly above the 65% noise bound, so the signal at that depth is weak.

assertions.value: The authors state that all training was done classically and that no claims of quantum advantage are made.
quotes: We reiterate that all of the training was done classically, so there are not claims of a quantum advantage here.
While no claims can be made about quantum advantage based on these results
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope in Sections 4.3 and 5.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Image Loading: Hierarchical Learning and Block-Amplitude Encoding
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section 3 loading results text, Section 5 hardware text, Section 6 Discussion; appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Hierarchical learning and block amplitude encoding to load MNIST and road-scene images into quantum states, with runs on IBM and Quantinuum hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that their methods train and implement image loading on 21 qubit circuits on existing quantum hardware, compared to 10 qubit circuits for MNIST.
quotes: Our methods allow us to train and implement image loading on 21 qubit circuits on existing quantum hardware, compared to the 10 qubit circuits for MNIST.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result from one study by the vendor authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that with a fixed 2-qubit gate count of 65 they achieve a larger fidelity than the earlier circuit library despite a more rigid circuit ansatz.
quotes: we load the same images with a pre-determined circuit structure for all digits and a fixed 2-qubit gate count of 65 to match. Quite generically, we achieve a larger fidelity despite a more rigid circuit ansatz.
assertions.certainty_reason: Comparison to an earlier circuit library on MNIST digits in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is on loading fidelity, not on downstream task accuracy.

assertions.value: The authors state that on hardware they probe only coarse-grained statistics of the loaded data as a sanity check, namely single Pauli Z expectation values.
quotes: we instead probe more coarse grained statistics of the data as a sanity check, namely single Pauli Z expectation values.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of how hardware loading was checked, Section 5.
assertions.reader_inference: Hardware loading is not shown to reproduce the full image distribution.

assertions.value: The authors state that they believe the hierarchical ansatz is an effective strategy for avoiding barren plateaus.
quotes: Ultimately, we believe the hierarchical ansatz is an effective strategy for avoiding barren plateaus
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a belief in the Discussion, without a proof in this paper.

papers.title_in_file: A variational hybrid continuous-variable discrete-variable quantum algorithm for adiabatic nuclear dynamics
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section III F limitations, Section IV Conclusion; algorithm derivations and appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A variational hybrid qubit-oscillator algorithm for simulating adiabatic nuclear dynamics, tested numerically and on a cavity-transmon device.

assertions.value: The authors describe the work as a proof-of-concept algorithm and state that the investigation pertains solely to one-dimensional models.
quotes: This work presents a proof-of-concept variational hybrid CV-DV algorithm for simulating adiabatic nuclear dynamics.
We note that our investigation pertains solely to one-dimensional models where the core properties of the algorithm can be highlighted.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Introduction as the paper's own scope.

assertions.value: The authors report that a single frozen-Gaussian variant was used to simulate the photoelectron spectrum of SO2 on physical quantum hardware, with variational parameters computed classically, and that the resulting simulated spectrum matches well with the experimental one.
quotes: A single FG variant of our algorithm was used to simulate the photoelectron spectrum of SO2 from physical quantum hardware.
The resulting simulated spectrum matches well with the experimental one.
assertions.certainty_reason: One molecule on a single-mode cavity device; parameters were computed on classical hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: Only the autocorrelation step ran on the quantum device; the variational optimization did not.

assertions.value: The authors report that the superposition variant converged to the numerically exact results in most cases as the number of Gaussians increased, and described wavepacket bifurcation in a double-well potential only moderately well.
quotes: The variant that evolves a superposition of FGs converged to the numerically exact results in most cases when increasing the number of FGs.
describe moderately well wavepacket bifurcation on a double-well potential.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical tests on simple one-dimensional models.

assertions.value: The authors state three limitations: the extremely high cost of stochastic circuit sampling, the lower expressivity of the ansatz compared to Gaussian wavepacket methods with free variational parameters, and the effect of the initial conditions.
quotes: we highlight three limitations of the algorithm: the extremely high cost of stochastic circuit sampling, the lower expressivity of our ansatz compared to GWP methods with free variational parameters, and the effect of the initial conditions
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limits, Section III F.

papers.version_note: File title is Harmonic (Quantum) Neural Networks, arXiv 2212.07462v2; it states the published version appears as Harmonic Neural Networks (ICML 2023). Same work as the record.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 3 results text, Section 4 Discussion; Section 2 derivations and appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Neural network and simulated quantum neural network constructions that give exactly or approximately harmonic functions, benchmarked against physics-informed networks.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate effective means of representing harmonic functions in neural networks and extend the results to quantum neural networks, and show favourable performance against (quantum) physics-informed neural networks.
quotes: we demonstrate effective means of representing harmonic functions in neural networks and extend such results also to quantum neural networks
We benchmark our approaches against (quantum) physics-informed neural networks, where we show favourable performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Benchmarks on a few physics problems in one study; the quantum networks were simulated.
assertions.reader_inference: Numbers are in Table 1 and were not read; the advantage is over PINN baselines.

assertions.value: The authors state that they construct exactly harmonic functions for simply-connected two-dimensional domains using complex-valued neural networks.
quotes: We demonstrate exactly-harmonic functions for simply-connected two-dimensional domains using complex-valued NNs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Construction derived in Section 2.1, stated in the Introduction.
assertions.reader_inference: Exact harmonicity holds in two dimensions only; higher dimensions are approximate.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not wish to compare classical and quantum neural networks, because the comparison is fraught with difficulties.
quotes: we do not wish to compare classical and quantum neural networks. The comparison is fraught with difficulties.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of scope in Section 3.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives no quantum advantage claim.

assertions.value: The authors report that their CurlNet architectures consistently achieve lower RMSEs than their PINN counterparts, while exhibiting higher errors in their Laplacians.
quotes: our CurlNet architectures consistently achieve lower RMSEs than their PINN counterparts, whilst exhibiting higher errors in their Laplacians
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on classical networks in one robot-navigation benchmark.
